title: The one-letter meter
hook: ajai alai abhai abai: unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging (Jaap, ek achhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, khal khanddan, and your line, break cruelty, adorn earth. Did you refuse one small cruelty? Today, Jaap's most compressed meter, where the words are almost all one sound. Day three hundred fifty-one.

Try this. Say ah. Just the sound, mouth open, nothing else. It's the sound at the doctor's office, the sound of relief when you sit down after a long day, the sound of surprise. In Gurmukhi, it has its own letter, airha, near the very start of the alphabet. Now put that sound at the front of almost every word in a stanza, and build the whole meter on it. Jaap Sahib has one. Today: the one-letter meter.
screen: `SAY AH.` → `A SOUND WITH ITS OWN LETTER.` → `A STANZA BUILT ON IT.`

segments.voice: The meter is called ek achhari. Ek is one, achhar is a letter. The one-letter meter. Sikh teachers explain the name in more than one way, but you can hear the plainest reason straight away: almost every word in these stanzas begins with the same letter, the a that means without. Here's the first line: ajai, alai, abhai, abai. Four words, four doors closing on four old fears. Ajai. Jai is victory, being conquered, so ajai is unconquerable. Nobody defeats the One. Alai. Lai is dissolving, being destroyed, so alai is indestructible. Nothing wipes the One away. Abhai. Bhai is fear, so abhai is fearless. Abai. Bai is age, wearing down, so abai is ageless, unchanging. Unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging. Listen to what's underneath that list. Defeat, destruction, fear, decay. Call them four shadows over a human life: losing, being wiped out, being afraid, getting old. And each one is answered with a single short a. It's almost the opposite of everything Jaap has said so far, the long names, the Persian titles, the doubled words. Here the praise gets very small, and very fast. Some reciters fly through these lines so quickly they sound like rain on a roof. The one-letter meter sounds like the hymn running out of room for anything but the essentials. And Jaap keeps coming back to one of these four in particular. Tomorrow, the one in the middle: abhai.
screen: `EK ACHHARI: THE ONE-LETTER METER.` · `AJAI: UNCONQUERABLE. ALAI: INDESTRUCTIBLE.` · `ABHAI: FEARLESS. ABAI: UNCHANGING.` · `FOUR SHADOWS, FOUR SHORT ANSWERS.` · then, large: `AJAI, ALAI, ABHAI, ABAI.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say the four words slowly. Ajai. Breathe. Alai. Breathe. Abhai. Breathe. Abai. Breathe. Let each one land. Then say them a little faster, the way they're recited, ajai, alai, abhai, abai, and feel the rhythm. Then stop, and sit with the open sound of a, the one at the front of every word. The bell holds the time.
Ek achhari. The one-letter meter, where nearly every word begins with a: ajai, alai, abhai, abai — unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging.
Your line: ajai, alai, abhai, abai. Today, when you feel beaten, worn down or afraid, say the four words once under your breath. Day three hundred fifty-one.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite the ek achhari stanzas near the end of Jaap Sahib very quickly, and many know the line ajai, alai, abhai, abai by heart.

fork.setup: defeat, destruction, fear and decay hang over every human life. how does the ek achhari line answer them?
options: with a long explanation of each.
with four short words: ajai, alai, abhai, abai.
fork.reveal: unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging: each shadow answered with a single small a, without.

original.note: Gurmukhi: the first line of Jaap's ek achhari, each word opening with the same letter.

trapdoor: what you thought: ajai, alai, abhai, abai is a tongue-twister.
what it means: four quick answers to defeat, destruction, fear and decay: unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging.
what a scholar hears: the ek achhari chhand compresses each epithet into the privative a- plus a monosyllabic root (jai, lai, bhai, bai).

sources.ref: Jaap Sahib, ek achhari chhand: ajai alai abhai abai

notes: The meaning of the name 'ek achhari' is explained in more than one way; the voice gives the plain reading (nearly every word starts with the same letter) and says explanations differ. Confirm.
Glosses: jai (victory/conquest), lai (dissolution), bhai (fear), bai (age/decay): confirm, especially abai.
Hook says Gurmukhi has a letter for the a-sound, airha (ਅ), right at the start of the alphabet (it is the second letter, after oorha ੳ). Confirm wording.
Gurmukhi ਅਜੈ ਅਲੈ ਅਭੈ ਅਬੈ: confirm spelling.
